correctness.rationale: For arbitrary fixed finite nonnegative lags and positive current populations, logistic and forced linear comparisons give positivity/global boundedness. For beta<d, y'≤beta*y(t-tau1)-d*y and beta<d give exponential comparison, then z decays exponentially. At beta=d, P=y+d∫_(t-tau1)^t y satisfies the exact dissipation P'=-d*m*y(t-tau1)^2/(x(t-tau1)+m*y(t-tau1))-theta*y*z/(v+p*y+q*z)≤0. The bounded denominator yields ∫y²<∞, and bounded derivative yields y→0, hence z exponential. Under r>b+alpha/m, lower logistic comparison bounds x away from zero and gives x→X=(r-b)/a. Writing h=-P', y'=d(y_del-y)-h, positivity bounds y_del≤e^(D*tau1)y≤e^(D*tau1)P, so h≤C(P²+zP). Q=1/P satisfies Q'≤C+C*z*Q; z integrable gives Q=O(t), yielding P≥c/(1+t), slow variation under bounded translations, and z/P→0. Normalized translates y(t_n+s)/P(t_n) converge subsequentially to bounded entire solutions Y'=d(Y(s-tau1)-Y), Y+d∫Y=1. Fourier symbol i*xi+d(1-e^(-i*xi*tau1)) has only real zero xi=0; bounded entire Y is constant 1/(1+d*tau1). Hence -P'/P²→d*m/[X*(1+d*tau1)²], and t*y→X*(1+d*tau1)/(d*m), including tau1=0. Independent exact SymPy algebra verified the dissipation, quadratic delay normal coefficient, and rational beta>d stable-equilibrium Jacobian (trace -11/8, determinant 17/16, remaining eigenvalue -1/2). Computation does not replace the global analytic argument.

value.rationale: The beta=d surface is a natural nonhyperbolic spectral threshold in a published three-species delay model; strict local stability fails to determine nonlinear global extinction or relaxation. The theorem supplies a structurally new nonnegative lag-compensated mass, closes the endpoint globally for all positive histories and finite fixed delays, obtains an exact positive leading amplitude depending linearly on gestation time, and exhibits an attracting positive-predator equilibrium for beta>d showing sharpness of the parameter-uniform extinction bound. These are motivated analytical dynamics facts with interpretable boundary behavior, not just a standard norm estimate, finite simulation or known equilibrium table. It does not claim stochastic/spatial/time-varying delay cases or classify all beta>d.
